bull.t: Rapid Revenue Growth and High Gross Margin
bull.b: Rapid revenue expansion and approximately 90% gross margin indicate improving product economics and growing commercial traction. If sustained, this combination can support operating leverage as sales scale, strengthen reinvestment capacity, and improve the company’s path toward future profitability.

A cash balance of approximately $220M provides meaningful funding for commercialization, regulatory work, and ongoing operations. This liquidity gives management time to evaluate which activities drive durable patient growth and reduces immediate pressure to secure additional financing.

Repeat purchasing among e-pharmacy patients offers an early indicator that VIZZ may generate recurring demand rather than one-time use. Combined with commercialization partnerships spanning more than 20 countries, this supports broader market access and a potentially scalable international platform.

bear.b: Large operating losses and substantially negative cash flow show that the business is not yet self-funding. Continued burn can reduce the cash reserve over time and may require external financing, while the scale of losses makes achieving sustainable profitability dependent on substantial operating improvement.

bear.t: Product Revenue Remains Small Versus Costs
bear.b: The wide gap between product revenue and operating expenses indicates that commercialization has not yet reached a scale capable of supporting the cost base. Until sales grow materially or spending is reduced, revenue growth may continue to coexist with significant losses and ongoing funding needs.

bear.t: Weak Retail Adoption and Prescribing Conversion
bear.b: Limited retail adoption restricts distribution breadth and reduces visibility into refill and persistence behavior outside e-pharmacy. The gap between awareness and recurring prescribing also suggests that converting professional familiarity into repeat demand remains an unresolved commercial challenge.
